data.gender_notes: Gershom is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gershom means 'stranger there' or 'sojourner in a foreign land' in Hebrew. In the Bible, it is the name given to Moses' firstborn son when the family lived in the land of Midian. The name Gershom carries the meaning “Sojourner in a foreign land” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Gershom usually hope their child will grow to embody sojourner in a foreign land and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey of faith and the search for a place to call home in God's divine plan.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gershom total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.long_meaning: Gershom, son of Moses, a Levite, or stranger, from Hebrew roots (, ), (, ). It signifies a foreigner or an alien, often associated with Moses' son, who was born during the Israelites' sojourn in Egypt. The name Gershom reflects the idea of being a stranger in a foreign land, which holds spiritual significance in Christian tradition, symbolizing the experience of being a believer in a world not our own.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gershom reflects the lived experience of enslavement and migration, as well as the challenges and possibilites of being a foreigner or an outcast in a new land. This name continues to resonate with contemporary communities who hold stories of displacement, exile, and migration close to their hearts. The name Gershom thus symbolizes resilience and adaptability in the face of cultural differences and adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gershom also holds deep spiritual significance as it echoes the Jewish Deliverance from slavery in Egypt and the call for the Israelites to enter into a covenant relationship with God. As Moses' firstborn son in a foreign land, Gershom represents a new beginning and a second chance, a reminder that even in the most challenging circumstances, God is present and willing to lead his people to a place of promise and redemption. This name inspires a sense of hope and faith, encouraging those who bear it to trust in the divine providence and to remain steadfast in their spiritual journeys.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gershom: "stranger there in a foreign land," reflecting the Israelites' sojourn in Egypt and their eventual return to their homeland. It serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness in guiding His people through their trials and leading them back to the Promised Land.

biblical_reference.note: Moses' son, Gershom, was born during the Israelites' sojourn in Egypt.

historical_references.reference: Gershom, the eldest son of Joseph and Asenath, is mentioned in Genesis 50:13 and is said to have been born in Egypt during Joseph's time as a slave and second-in-command to Pharaoh. Gershom means 'having come from a foreign land' in Hebrew.

Gershom, a 13th century German theologian and mystic, is known for his work 'The Book of the Garden of the Pure Love'. He taught that God's presence could be experienced in all things and that union with the divine was attainable through the practice of contemplation and the development of the inner self.
